records.title: Evaluation of four different exercise types for use in altitude decompression sickness studies
records.authors: Fischer MD, Wiegman JF, McLean SA, Olson RM, Pilmanis AA
records.note: Thirteen participants were reported for workload selection. Four additional sessions verified work loads over repeated 12-minute bouts. A separate count of verification participants and dispersion for the four means are unavailable. The 1999 paper cites this method and reports its own 370 mL/min overall mean in Table I. Individual linkage is unavailable.

records.title: Venous gas emboli detection and endpoints for decompression sickness research
records.note: The authors give about 65 percent agreement for a retrospective Armstrong archive comparison of Doppler VGE and clinical DCS. The abstract supplies no denominator, confusion matrix or independent validation. A proposed joint-pain and function scale is described. The two SAFE outlets are cited under the same title in the reprint.

records.title: Monitoring cognitive function and need with the automated neuropsychological assessment metrics in decompression sickness research
records.locator: SOAR proceedings, printed p. 498, N94-11533. Armstrong reprint, printed pp. 17–18 (PDF pp. 23–24)
records.note: The original NASA page uses Need in its title. The Armstrong reprint uses Mood. Authors, year, printed page and body identify the same abstract. Methods concern cognitive and mood monitoring for a four-hour simulated 30,000-ft protocol. Participants and clinical outcomes are unreported. The same approximate Armstrong archive agreement is repeated as background.

records.title: Use of echo imaging in decompression model development
records.authors: Olson RM, Pilmanis AA, Scoggins TE
records.locator: AsMA abstract 9, printed p. 386 (PDF p. 2). Armstrong reprint, printed pp. 19–20 (PDF pp. 25–26)
records.note: Three male participants at 29,500 ft with heart and inferior vena cava imaging. The reported 5–100 micrometre estimate concerns the vena cava and hepatic veins. Flight count, clinical event totals and crosswalk to the four-person and later ten-person reports are unavailable.

records.authors: Olson RM, Pilmanis AA, Scoggins TE
records.note: The SAFE summary gives four examined decompressed participants. There is no complete flight or symptom count and no identifiers to verify overlap with the three-person AsMA or ten-person technical report samples.

records.title: Decompression sickness protection using a 100% oxygen pressure suit environment
records.locator: AsMA abstract 6, printed p. 386 (PDF p. 2). Armstrong reprint, printed p. 29 (PDF p. 35)
records.note: The preliminary three male groups use the same pressure, planned time, gas, prebreathe, activity and severe VGE margins as the three published journal groups. NEDU Appendix E lists 11 male exposures for the 7.3-psia profile, compared with 10 in the meeting abstract and journal. Membership of the additional compiled exposure is unresolved.

records.title: The effect of differences in time to detection of circulating microbubbles on the risk of decompression sickness
records.note: The publisher version matches the NTRS title, byline, protocol and 17 symptomatic exposures among 81 already recorded in v1.120. This occurrence verifies the original meeting edition and contributes no separately counted observations.
